stories.headline: Australia's fuel security diplomacy intensifies as Wong heads to North Asia and Albanese warns of 'long tail' of war
stories.summary: With Australia at Level 2 of its national fuel security plan amid the US-Iran war's disruption to Strait of Hormuz shipping, Prime Minister Albanese conducted a diplomatic tour of Southeast Asia (Singapore, Malaysia, Brunei, Vietnam) and Foreign Minister Wong departed Sunday for a week of talks in Japan, China and South Korea. The government is also underwriting fertiliser cargoes and discussing a new domestic oil refinery, as officials warn Australians of lasting economic impacts.

stories.headline: AUKUS submarine program faces scrutiny as US awards first major contract but delivery doubts persist
stories.summary: The United States awarded a $197 million contract to Electric Boat under the AUKUS pact, described as the first major financial commitment to materialise from the agreement. Simultaneously, the Pentagon's new submarine chief acknowledged US Navy production capacity remains behind schedule, France offered to sell submarines if AUKUS collapses, and debate intensified in Australia about whether the program remains fit for purpose given shifting strategic priorities and new detection technology.

stories.headline: Taylor's 'values-based' immigration policy and 'bad countries' remarks dominate opposition week
stories.summary: Opposition Leader Angus Taylor drew sustained criticism and controversy after doubling down on his coalition's immigration policy, which includes an 'Australian values test' for migrants and warnings about 'bad people from bad countries.' Taylor also partially blamed the 'overuse' of Welcome to Country ceremonies for Anzac Day booing incidents in Melbourne, Perth and Sydney, while Pauline Hanson addressed an anti-immigration rally in Canberra. The policy debate is unfolding against the backdrop of the Farrer by-election.

stories.headline: Albanese government rejects windfall gas export tax amid fuel crisis pressure
stories.summary: The Albanese government decided against pursuing a new windfall gas export levy in the upcoming May budget, with independent senator David Pocock accusing the government of 'caving to gas companies' and parroting industry talking points. The decision was influenced in part by the fuel supply crisis sparked by the US-Iran war, and the International Energy Agency warned against sudden tax changes that could spook investors.

stories.headline: RBA widely expected to raise rates again in May as war-driven inflation heats up
stories.summary: Markets and economists are pricing in another Reserve Bank of Australia rate hike at the May meeting, driven by surging fuel prices linked to the US-Iran conflict. The RBA has already hiked twice in 2026, major banks including Westpac are lifting fixed rates ahead of the meeting, and a key March CPI reading due Wednesday is expected to show further inflation pressure.

stories.headline: Albanese joins world leaders in condemning White House Correspondents' Dinner shooting
stories.summary: Prime Minister Albanese issued a statement praising the US Secret Service and expressing relief after an armed man disrupted the White House Correspondents' Dinner in Washington, injuring a Secret Service agent. Albanese also texted President Trump directly. Multiple international outlets reported the Australian PM's response as part of global leader reaction coverage.

stories.headline: NDIS overhaul announced, Coalition signals support despite state backlash over new disability definitions
stories.summary: Health Minister Mark Butler announced sweeping changes to the National Disability Insurance Scheme, including removing around 160,000 people from eligibility and redefining 'permanent' disability. Opposition Leader Taylor indicated the Coalition would support the overhaul, while disability advocates and some state ministers warned the new eligibility criteria would be 'impossible' to implement and would abandon those in need.

stories.headline: Anzac Day commemorated at Gallipoli and across Australia amid Welcome to Country booing controversy
stories.summary: Australia and New Zealand observed the 111th anniversary of the Battle of Gallipoli at ceremonies in Turkey, while domestically Anzac Day dawn services in Melbourne, Sydney and Perth were disrupted by booing directed at Indigenous presenters delivering Welcome to Country addresses. One man was arrested. Defence Minister Marles described the behaviour as 'disgraceful,' while Albanese published a reflection on the Anzac legacy.

stories.headline: Australian ISIS-linked families attempt repatriation from Syrian camp, stoking political controversy
stories.summary: Four Australian families with alleged links to Islamic State militants left Roj Camp in eastern Syria in a second repatriation attempt facilitated by Syrian authorities. Opposition Leader Taylor called on the government to prevent their return and accused it of failing to use available powers, while also avoiding questions about whether he trusted ASIO's assessments of the threat.

stories.headline: Bondi Beach shooting royal commission: AFP and ASIO cleared in internal reviews but scrutiny continues
stories.summary: Internal reviews by the Australian Federal Police and ASIO cleared both agencies of responsibility for failing to prevent the Bondi Beach attack, with investigators concluding the suspected motivation was the Gaza war. However, the findings will still be tested before the ongoing royal commission, and former ASIO director Dennis Richardson's earlier resignation as a special adviser has raised questions about how seriously agencies responded when the terror threat level was raised in 2024.
